The best multivitamins and minerals 2026 – tried and tested

What are the best multivitamin and mineral supplements, and are they worth it? Find out who may benefit from taking a multivitamin, and which nutrients should be included in a multi

Multivitamin and mineral supplements combine a range of vitamins and minerals in one product and are commonly used to support everyday health. If you’re looking for the best multivitamin, it’s worth knowing there’s no standard formula. Ingredients and nutrient levels can vary widely between brands, making it harder to compare multivitamin tablets and capsules or know exactly what you’re getting. Which in some cases, can be an issue.

A balanced and varied diet is the first step towards getting the vitamins and minerals your body needs. Vitamins D, C and K, iron, fibre, zinc and omega-3, for example, all play a role in supporting mental and physical health.

However, national surveys show that we can fall short of recommended intakes for a range of nutrients. Over time, this may be a risk factor for chronic disease, particularly among older people. A well-chosen supplement may help some people top up their intake.

Do I need to take a multivitamin?

Many multivitamins and mineral supplements available on the high street are generally considered safe. Supplements are not a substitute for a balanced diet, but some evidence suggests they may help address gaps in nutrient intake.

Deciding whether to take a multivitamin can be difficult, especially as some studies have found no association between supplementation and improved health outcomes. Comparing the research is challenging because studies use different definitions of a multivitamin, vary the nutrient doses and test formulations that can change over time. item.title: Slow cooker gammon in cola
item.description:

Why it is here: useful and clear, with a fresh angle

Slow cooker gammon in cola

Fill your kitchen with the smell of Christmas with this gammon, made in the slow cooker. The cola adds a sweet treacly flavour to balance the saltiness of the ham.

- 1.5-1.8kg unsmoked boneless gammon joint

- 2l cola(not diet)

- 1 carrotpeeled and chopped

- 1 onionpeeled and quartered

- 1 stick celerychopped

- 1 cinnamon stick

- ½ tbsp peppercorns

- 1 bay leaf

For the glaze

- 150ml maple syrup

- 2 tbsp wholegrain mustard

- 2 tbsp red wine vinegar

- pinch of ground clovesor five-spice

- kcal329

- fat15g

- saturates5g

- carbs16g

- sugars14g

- fibre1g

- protein33g

- salt4.3g

Method

- step 1 Set your slow cooker to medium. Place the gammon joint in and cover with the cola. Add 1 chopped carrot, 1 quartered onion, 1 chopped celery stick, 1 cinnamon stick, ½ tbsp peppercorns and 1 bay leaf.

- step 2 Cook for 5½ hrs on low until the gammon is tender but still holding its shape, topping up with boiling water if necessary to keep the gammon fully covered.

- step 3 Carefully pour the liquid away, then let the ham cool a little while you heat the oven to 190C/170C fan/gas 5. Lift the ham into a roasting tin, then cut away the skin leaving behind an even layer of fat. Score the fat all over in a criss-cross pattern.

- step 4 Mix the maple syrup, mustard, vinegar and ground cloves or five-spice in a jug. Pour half over the fat, roast for 15 mins, then pour over the rest and return to the oven for another 30 mins.

- step 5 Remove from the oven and allow to rest for 10 mins, then spoon more glaze over the top. Can be roasted on the day or up to two days ahead and served cold.

item.title: Ferrero Rocher Blossom Cookies
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: original and detailed, with a unique twist

Ferrero Rocher Blossom Cookies

Chocolate hazelnut lovers, these Ferrero Rocher blossom cookies are for you! They take classic thumbprint cookies to a whole new level of flavor and texture.

Chocolate-hazelnut lovers, you might want to sit down for this one. These Ferrero Rocher blossom cookies aren’t your average thumbprint cookies. We’re talking rich chocolate cookies rolled in crunchy chopped hazelnuts, filled with a gooey dollop of Nutella and finished with an entire Ferrero Rocher chocolate perched on top. They’re a little over the top in the very best way.

Every bite is a delicious mix of soft, crunchy, creamy, chocolatey and nutty. They’re almost too pretty to eat (almost!), and they’re guaranteed to steal the show at a holiday cookie exchange. They make a pretty impressive homemade gift, too. Just be prepared for everyone to ask for the recipe.

Ingredients for Ferrero Rocher Blossom Cookies

- Butter: Start with softened butter so it creams easily with the sugar. And don’t skimp on the creaming time! Beating the butter and sugar for at least five minutes incorporates tiny air pockets into the dough, resulting in light, tender cookies.

- Sugar: Granulated white sugar sweetens the cookie dough and crisps up the cookie edges.

- Egg: You’ll need to separate an egg for these cookies. The yolk adds richness and tenderness to the cookie dough, while the white helps the chopped hazelnuts stick to the outside. Let the egg come to room temperature before starting so it blends easily into the dough.

- Milk: A splash of milk adds moisture and brings the chocolate cookie dough together. Any kind of milk you have in the fridge will work.

- Vanilla: A little vanilla extract enhances the chocolate and hazelnut flavors.

- Flour: Nothing fancy needed here! Be sure to spoon regular all-purpose flour into your measuring cup and level it off rather than scooping straight from the bag.

- Baking cocoa: This is what gives the cookies their rich chocolate flavor! Reach for unsweetened cocoa powder, not hot chocolate mix, which has added sugar and other ingredients.

- Hazelnuts: Toast the hazelnuts before chopping them to bring out their flavor, then let them cool completely before rolling the cookie dough balls in them.

- Chocolate hazelnut spread: Nutella is the classic choice, but any chocolate-hazelnut spread will work. It creates a slightly gooey filling in the center of each cookie, and acts as the glue that holds the chocolate candy in place.

- Ferrero Rocher chocolates: These individually wrapped chocolate-hazelnut candies are the finishing touch. Each one is a whole hazelnut enrobed in creamy filling and a crisp chocolate-and-hazelnut shell. Unwrap the candies before the cookies come out of the oven so they’re ready to be pressed into the warm centers.

Directions

Step 1: Make the cookie dough

In a large bowl, cream the butter and sugar with a handheld mixer until they’re light and fluffy, five to seven minutes. Beat in the egg yolk, milk and vanilla.

In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the creamed mixture, mixing until a soft dough forms. Cover and refrigerate the dough for about one hour, or until it’s firm enough to handle.

Editor’s Tip: Don’t skip chilling the dough. It makes it easier to roll into balls and helps the cookies hold their shape as they bake.

Step 2: Shape the cookies

Preheat the oven to 350°F. In a small bowl, whisk the egg white until it’s foamy. Shape the chilled dough into 1-1/2-inch balls. Dip the balls into the egg white, letting any excess drip off, then roll them in the chopped hazelnuts to coat.

Arrange the dough balls on greased baking sheets. Use the end of a wooden spoon handle to gently press an indentation into the center of each cookie.

Step 3: Bake the cookies

Bake the cookies for 13 to 15 minutes, or until the centers of the cookies are set.

Step 4: Fill the cookies

While the cookies are still warm, spoon or pipe a small dollop of Nutella into each indentation. Gently press an unwrapped Ferrero Rocher chocolate into the center of each cookie.

Carefully transfer the cookies from the baking sheets to wire racks to cool completely.

Editor’s Tip: A piping bag or small zip-top bag with one corner snipped off makes it easy to add the Nutella neatly to the centers.

Recipe Variations

- Switch up the nuts: No hazelnuts in the pantry? Finely chopped almonds, pecans or walnuts all make a delicious crunchy coating. You can also skip the nuts and roll the dough balls in granulated sugar instead.

- Try a different filling: Replace the regular chocolate-hazelnut spread with Nutella Peanut, plain peanut butter, cookie butter or another chocolaty spread. Just keep in mind that swapping the filling will change the flavor of the finished cookies.

- Add a flavor boost: Stir 1 teaspoon of instant espresso powder—the secret ingredient for better chocolate treats—into the dry ingredients to deepen the chocolate flavor without making the cookies taste like coffee.

- Swap the candy: Instead of Ferrero Rocher chocolates, press a chocolate kiss, chocolate truffle or mini peanut butter cup into the warm cookies. It’s an easy way to make several varieties from one batch of dough.

How to Store Ferrero Rocher Blossom Cookies

Let the cookies cool completely, then transfer them to an airtight cookie storage container. Store them at room temperature in a cool, dry place for up to five days. If you need to stack them, place a sheet of parchment or wax paper between layers to protect the chocolate toppings.

Can you make chocolate hazelnut cookies ahead of time?

Absolutely! These cookies stay fresh for several days when stored properly, so you can bake them a day or two before serving.

You can also prepare the cookie dough up to two days in advance and keep it covered in the refrigerator. When you’re ready to bake, let the dough sit at room temperature for a few minutes, then shape, coat and bake the cookies as directed.…

Why it is here: well-written, but not as informative as others

Mistletoe Martini

A mistletoe martini is holiday sparkle you can sip. It tastes like a frosty-cold vodka-cranberry with added floral notes, and the most festive garnish you can dream of.

The mistletoe martini is the perfect spirited sipper for your holiday parties. It’s flavored with cranberry—a classic December flavor—but adds elderflower liqueur and a little simple syrup for a French kiss of floral sweetness. A hard shake turns the concoction into a cocktail that feels way fancier than the effort it takes.

You don’t have to be a bartender or jolly old St. Nick to whip one up. The hardest part is the garnish, and even that is just a couple of sage leaves cozied up between two cranberries on a pick. Just don’t garnish it with actual mistletoe, no matter how hard you’re angling for a smooch, because mistletoe is toxic. Let it work its magic from the doorway, not your glass! Shake up a mistletoe martini for yourself after a long night of gift wrapping, or batch a pitcher and make it the most kissable drink in your lineup of Christmas cocktails.

Mistletoe Martini Ingredients

- Cranberry juice: Cranberry juice gives this cocktail its festive ruby color and the tart backbone that keeps it from tasting like candy.

- Vodka: Vodka is the clean, neutral base that lets the cranberry and elderflower do the talking. A good mid-range bottle you’d happily sip is perfect, so save the top-shelf vodka brand for a classic martini.

- Elderflower liqueur: This French liqueur is made from elderflower blossoms, and tastes floral and lightly sweet with notes of pear, lychee and citrus. A few well-known brands include St-Germain, St. Elder and Giffard.

- Simple syrup: Simple syrup is just sugar dissolved in water. It balances the tart cranberry juice. You can buy it bottled, but it takes about five minutes to prep homemade simple syrup.

- Sage leaves: Fresh sage adds a woodsy, savory aroma, and its soft green color looks gorgeous against the red drink. Choose bright, perky leaves without any brown spots or wilting.

- Cranberries: Fresh cranberries skewered on a pick turn this drink into a tiny holiday decoration.

Directions

Step 1: Fill the shaker

Fill a shaker with ice.

Step 2: Add the ingredients

Add the vodka, cranberry juice, elderflower liqueur and simple syrup.

Editor’s Tip: If you’re not sure how sweet your cranberry juice is, start with half the simple syrup and add more to taste.

Step 3: Shake the cocktail

Shake hard until the liquid is very cold and the shaker is frosty, about 10 to 15 seconds.

Step 4: Strain the cocktail over fresh ice

Strain the cocktail and pour it over fresh ice into a cocktail glass.

Editor’s Tip: Pop your glasses in the freezer for 10 to 15 minutes before guests arrive so they stay frosty longer.

Step 5: Garnish and serve

Garnish the cocktail with a couple of sage leaves between two cranberries on a cocktail pick. Lay the pick across the rim of the glass or let it rest in the drink. Serve the cocktail right away while it’s cold.

Editor’s Tip: Before you skewer the sage, gently clap the leaves between your palms to release their aroma. It’s an old bartender trick that makes every sip smell like the holidays.

Mistletoe Martini Variations

- Switch up the spirit: Swap gin for the vodka to add some botanical flair. The juniper and herbal notes play very nicely with the sage garnish.

- Jazz up the juice: There are a zillion different cranberry juice blends out there made with cherry, raspberry and apple juice, so pick whichever one suits your fancy. Know that ones with added flavors may result in a sweeter mistletoe martini. Trader Joe’s Wassail Punch is a fun choice too.

- Get creative with the garnish: Spike cranberries on rosemary twigs, freeze the cranberries and float them on top of the drink, or tie up a little bundle of mint. Your imagination is the limit.

- Serve it up: Skip the fresh ice and strain the cocktail into a chilled coupe or martini glass for a more classic martini presentation. It feels a little more elegant for a holiday dinner party.

How to Store Mistletoe Martinis

A shaken mistletoe martini is best enjoyed right away, since ice keeps melting and diluting the drink the longer it sits. The good news is that this drink can easily be made into a batched cocktail, by mixing the base ahead of time and keeping it in the fridge until the party starts. Just leave out the ice and the garnish until you’re ready to serve.

Can you make a batch of mistletoe martinis ahead of time?

You can make mistletoe martinis ahead of time by mixing a big batch of the base in a pitcher. For eight drinks, stir together 2 cups of cranberry juice, 2 cups of vodka, 1 cup of elderflower liqueur and 1 cup of simple syrup, then chill it for at least a few hours. When guests arrive, you can shake individual portions with ice or you can dilute the base by stirring about 1 cup of cold water into the pitcher before pouring it over fresh ice. Skewer your garnishes a few hours ahead and keep them covered in the fridge so the sage stays fresh.

How long does a batch of mistletoe martini last?

A batched mistletoe martini base lasts up to three days in a covered pitcher or jar in the refrigerator. Give it a good stir before serving, since the ingredients can settle.

Mistletoe Martini Tips

What kind of cranberry juice is best for a mistletoe martini?

The best cranberry juice for a mistletoe martini depends on how sweet you like your cocktails, and you’ll want to adjust the simple syrup to match. Unsweetened, pure cranberry juice is super tart, so use the full ounce of simple syrup if you go this route. A 100% juice blend gets its sweetness from other juices like apple or grape, so start with 1/2 ounce to 3/4 ounce of syrup. Cranberry juice cocktail—the classic bar ingredient—already has added sugar, so start with 1/4 ounce of simple syrup, or skip it entirely. Whichever bottle you grab, taste the cocktail as you go.

item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-trimmed version. An LLM deleted boilerplate sentences from the original article and left the rest verbatim. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: good writing, but less informative and less unique

Fluffernutter Cookies

These fluffernutter cookies taste just like the classic lunchbox sandwich. Soft peanut butter cookies are swirled with gooey marshmallow fluff for a fun-for-all-ages treat.

Move over, peanut butter blossoms! There’s a new peanut butter cookie in town. These fluffernutter cookies bring together two childhood favorites—peanut butter and marshmallow fluff—in one soft, chewy cookie. If you grew up on the classic sandwich and still crave it, you’re going to love that same sweet-and-salty combination in cookie form.

Ingredients for Fluffernutter Cookies

- Shortening: Butter-flavored shortening adds a little extra buttery flavor while keeping the cookies soft and tender. Regular shortening works, too, so there’s no need to make a special trip to the store if you have it.

- Peanut butter: Creamy peanut butter gives these cookies their signature nutty flavor and makes the dough easy to work with. Stick with conventional peanut butter rather than natural, which can be a little too oily for this recipe.

- Sugar: You’ll need both granulated and brown sugar. White sugar adds sweetness, while brown sugar brings moisture and chewiness to the cookies.

- Eggs: Eggs help bind the dough. Bringing them to room temperature before making the cookie dough will help them mix more smoothly.

- Vanilla: A splash of vanilla rounds out the sweetness and adds subtle warmth.

- Flour: All-purpose flour gives the cookies structure. Spoon it into the measuring cup and level it off to avoid packing in too much.

- Baking soda: This leavening agent helps the cookies spread and gives them a tender texture.

- Salt: A full teaspoon balances the sweetness of the sugars and marshmallow fluff and brings out the peanut butter flavor. Don’t skip it!

- Marshmallow Fluff: Also known as marshmallow creme, this sweet, spreadable filling gives these cookies their signature gooey centers. Regular marshmallows can work in a pinch, but they won’t give you quite the same creamy filling.

Directions

Step 1: Make the cookie dough

Preheat the oven to 350°F. In a large bowl, cream the shortening, peanut butter and sugars until they’re light and fluffy, five to seven minutes. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in the vanilla.

In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the creamed mixture, mixing until they’re combined.

Step 2: Fill and shape the cookies

Scoop the dough by tablespoonfuls and arrange the portions on a parchment-lined baking sheet or work surface. Use your palms or the bottom of a drinking glass to flatten each scoop into a disk.

Pipe or spoon about 1 teaspoon of marshmallow fluff onto the center of half the disks, leaving a little space around the edges. Top each with another dough disk, pinching the edges together to seal in the filling.

Gently roll the filled cookies between your palms to smooth the edges, then flatten them slightly. Arrange the cookies 2 inches apart on parchment-lined baking sheets.

Editor’s Tip: A piping bag or zip-top bag with the corner snipped off makes it easy to add neat, even dollops of marshmallow fluff. If using a spoon, lightly coat it with cooking spray to help the sticky marshmallow release.

Step 3: Bake and cool

Bake until the edges are set and the cookies are lightly browned, 12 to 15 minutes. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring them to wire racks to cool completely.

Editor’s Tip: For perfectly shaped cookies, place a large round cookie cutter or glass over each cookie immediately after taking it out of the oven. Gently swirl it around the cookie to nudge the edges into a neat circle while the cookies are still warm and soft.

Recipe Variations

- Add a little sparkle: Roll the filled cookie dough balls in granulated sugar before baking them for a sparkly finish and a little crunch around the edges.

- Switch up the nut butter: Replace the peanut butter with creamy almond butter or cashew butter for a different nutty flavor. Choose a conventional, no-stir variety for the best texture.

- Try a pinch of cinnamon: Mix 1/2 teaspoon of ground cinnamon into the dry ingredients for a subtle warmth that makes these peanut butter cookies taste a little like a snickerdoodle and fluffernutter mashup.

How to Store Fluffernutter Cookies

Once completely cooled, store the fluffernutter cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to five days. If stacking them, place parchment paper between the layers to keep the marshmallow from sticking.

Can you freeze fluffernutter cookies?

Yes! For the best results, freeze the unfilled cookie dough balls rather than the assembled cookies. Arrange the dough balls on a parchment-lined baking sheet and freeze until firm, then transfer to a freezer-safe bag or container for up to three months.

When you’re ready to bake, thaw the dough in the refrigerator, flatten it into disks and add the marshmallow fluff as directed. Seal the cookies, shape them and bake them according to the recipe.

Fluffernutter Cookies Tips

What’s the best type of peanut butter to use for cookies?

Creamy, conventional peanut butter is your best bet for baking these fluffernutter cookies. Brands like Jif or Skippy have a consistent texture that makes the dough easy to mix and shape. Natural peanut butter tends to separate, which can make the dough too oily or crumbly. Save the fancy stuff for your morning toast!

Can you use regular marshmallows instead of creme?

Yes! While marshmallow creme gives these cookies their signature gooey center, you can use mini marshmallows instead. Place four or five mini marshmallows in the center of each dough disk, then top them with another disk and pinch the edges to seal them. The marshmallows will melt as the cookies bake, giving you little gooey pockets in every bite.
